logline: 마 캐던 소년이 노래 하나로 공주를 얻고 금 골짜기로 왕이 된다
destination: 설화 서동과 선화공주에서 만날 수 있습니다
setting: 백제의 못가와 신라 서라벌, 두 나라의 길
anchor: a Korean boy of about ten in hemp clothes, his small sister beside him
palette: earth red-brown, reed green, warm gold, indigo, cream

beats.visual: the reedy pond in slanting morning light: the boy kneels on the red-brown terrace with a wooden hoe, levering a long pale yam whole out of the dug earth, his hemp jacket dusty at the knees, easy wide grin at the size of the catch; beside him an A-frame carrier already stacked with washed yams, dragonflies hanging over the still water below, wild yam vines climbing the terrace stones; his quick clever eyes are on the prize but his short topknot is cocked toward the road beyond the pond — a boy who digs with his hands and travels with his thoughts
beats.motion: the hoe levers and the long yam eases whole out of the crumbling red earth, roots trailing fine soil, and the boy's grin widens as he lifts it high to judge it against the light; a dragonfly tilts past the raised yam, loose earth trickling back into the hole, and the camera stays low along the dug terrace with the pond shining behind

beats.visual: dusk at the pond's edge, the day's digging done: the boy sits on the loaded A-frame with a half-eaten yam, listening hard to two passing peddlers resting their packs by the water — their hands sketching the far direction of Silla over the hills, their talk plainly of the capital and of the king's third daughter; the boy's easy grin has gone thoughtful, clever eyes fixed on the darkening eastern hills, the yam forgotten mid-bite; reeds lean in the evening air, the first star stands over the terraces, and a plan is visibly being born on a dusty boy's face
beats.motion: the peddlers' hands sketch the eastward road over the hills while the boy's chewing slows and stops, his eyes lifting from their gestures to the darkening ridgeline and staying there; the half-eaten yam lowers by degrees to his knee, reeds leaning in the last light, and the camera closes slowly on the thinking face against the evening hills

beats.visual: a bright lane in Seorabeol: the boy crouches at his opened A-frame with a heap of pale yams, handing them out free to three village children — two boys and a girl, cheeks already full, bare feet dancing with the windfall — while his own grin works with more purpose than generosity; persimmon trees lean over the rammed-earth walls, a stone gutter runs bright down the lane's middle, tiered pagoda roofs rise far off; he is teaching them something between bites, his hand keeping steady patient time, and three small mouths are learning words along with the yam
beats.motion: his hand keeps time in small patient beats while the three children chew and nod and mumble the lines back, the girl catching the tune first and the boys tumbling after; another yam passes from the heap to a small reaching hand, persimmon leaves ticking over the wall, and the camera circles the little singing school at crouching height

beats.visual: the lane at play hour, the song let loose: the three children skip along the stone gutter singing at the top of their lungs, arms swinging, the girl leading with her chin high — and down the lane other children are catching it, two more joining from a gateway, another leaning off a wall, the mischievous verse about the princess and the yam-boy bouncing from wall to wall; a grandmother at a gate turns her head, a water-carrier grins mid-stride, persimmon leaves drift onto the singers, and the song is plainly no longer anyone's to stop
beats.motion: the three skip and sing down the gutter line and the song spreads visibly — a gate child joining on the second line, the wall-percher swinging his legs in time, the water-carrier's shoulders bouncing as he walks — arms swinging wider as the chorus grows; drifting leaves spin in their wake, and the camera tracks ahead of the growing parade of small singers

beats.visual: the Silla palace hall, the song arrived where songs should not go: the king stands risen from his dais, stern broad face darkening, jade pendants of his tall gold crown swinging with the sharp turn of his head — while below, a court official on both knees repeats the verse with his forehead nearly to the polished floor, every syllable clearly costing him a year of life; bronze lamps burn steady along the red pillars, silk screens hold their painted calm behind the dais, and somewhere beyond the walls, faint as weather, children's voices carry the tune past the palace itself
beats.motion: the kneeling official's recitation trails off into the floorboards while the king's head turns slowly toward the outer wall, jade pendants swinging and settling, his stern face darkening by shades as the faint children's tune drifts in on the air; lamp flames stand very straight, the painted screens hold still, and the camera rises slowly from the bowed official to the listening king

beats.visual: the palace's tall side gate at grey dawn: the princess steps out in plain traveling clothes — undyed jacket, grey skirt, one braid down her back, the single gold flower pin kept at her collar — a small cloth bundle on her back and her serene face held level against the morning cold; behind her the red pillars and green brackets of the hall recede in mist, two silent guards flank the gate looking straight ahead, and before her the road runs south between wet fields toward hills she has never walked; her step off the gate stone is small, unhurried and unbowed
beats.motion: she steps down from the gate stone and walks out along the field road at a steady unhurried pace, the bundle settling on her back, her braid swinging softly, breath faint in the cold air; the two guards hold their forward stare as the gate closes by degrees behind her, mist drifting over the wet fields ahead, and the camera follows her first quiet steps into exile

beats.visual: a bend of an unpaved dirt track between pines, pale packed earth and pine-needle verges with no pavement anywhere: the boy is the one kneeling — down on both knees in the road dust, hands flat before him, head lowered deep, waist bent to the ground, his hemp jacket brushed clean and topknot retied — while the princess is the one standing, a pace short of him in her plain traveling clothes, bundle at her back, serene face tilted down at the kneeling stranger with more curiosity than alarm; his A-frame waits set aside against a pine, a magpie watches from a bough, pine shadows bar the pale earth between them, and the dirt track runs on south behind the two figures deciding whether to share it
beats.motion: his lowered posture holds steady in the road dust, hands flat and head low, while her tilted gaze travels from the brushed jacket to the retied topknot to the flat honest hands — and her held breath eases into the beginning of a smile; the magpie hops one branch closer, pine shadows trembling across the pale earth between them, and the camera holds level on the standing princess and the kneeling boy

beats.visual: an evening mountain path, the two walking together at last: the boy ahead with his A-frame carrying her small bundle atop his yams, glancing back mid-story with his wide grin, and the princess a step behind, plain skirt gathered from the dew grass, laughing openly now with a hand at her mouth; the path winds between pines glowing rust in the late light, a stream runs somewhere below, and the space between the two travelers has closed from a wary pace to an easy arm's length; her gold flower pin catches the last sun at her collar, his stories plainly getting better the further they walk
beats.motion: he walks half-turned, hands sketching some tall moment of his story, and her laugh spills free behind her hand as she keeps pace, the gap between them easing shorter with the path's winding; the pines glow and darken by degrees, the stream sounding below, and the camera follows the two of them at story-telling distance down the winding light

beats.visual: a rest by a stream crossing, the story's hinge: the princess holds out on her open palm a lump of raw gold the size of a bird's egg — kept from her palace life for the road ahead — her face grave with the weight of their only wealth; and across the flat stone from her the boy is laughing, honestly and hugely, head back, hand slapping his knee, the laugh of someone shown a pebble from a beach he owns; her gravity tips into bewilderment, the gold sits small and bright between them on her palm, and the stream runs loud past the mismatched pair and their opposite understandings of treasure
beats.motion: her open palm holds the gold steady while his laugh rolls on, head back, hand coming down on his knee, and her grave face tips by degrees into bewildered half-smiling protest; the stream glitters past the flat stone, the gold catching one bright point of sun between them, and the camera closes on the palm and the laughing boy beyond it

beats.visual: on the yam terrace above the reedy pond in evening light: the boy standing at the left with one arm raised, pointing across the slope where fist-sized lumps of yellow metal lie half buried among the red-brown earth and yam vines; the princess standing a step to the right with both hands pressed to her mouth, her bundle slipped to the grass at her feet; exactly two people, one boy and one young woman, each with two arms
beats.motion: the boy's pointing arm sweeps slowly across the slope and the lumps glint one after another among the vines, the princess's hands staying pressed to her mouth; the camera holds on the two on the terrace

beats.visual: the Seorabeol road at bright midday: a line of ox-carts rolls toward the walls of the capital, each cart heaped with gold under lashed straw mats, corners of treasure glinting through — and walking at the head of the line the boy and the princess side by side, he with his old A-frame carrying nothing but her small bundle, she in her plain road clothes with the gold flower pin bright at her collar; gate guards crane from the wall, market people line the verge whispering behind hands, and the pair walk their gift in through the gates of the kingdom that exiled her
beats.motion: the ox-carts roll in a slow heavy line, straw mats shifting to flash gold at every rut, while the two at the head keep their easy walking pace through the widening whispers of the crowd; the gate guards straighten one after another as the line passes under the wall, and the camera walks with the pair through the opening gates

beats.visual: the Baekje throne hall in warm incense light: the boy — older in bearing now, hemp exchanged for a plain dark court robe but the quick clever eyes and easy grin unchanged — stands before the phoenix-carved throne receiving the bows of officials in white and violet along both walls; incense smoke climbs the warm ochre pillars, and at the hall's heart, seated where he can see her, the princess in crimson silk again with her gold flowers back in her braids — exile turned to honor beside the yam-digger turned lord; the throne waits one step above them both in the drifting sweet smoke
beats.motion: the officials' bows travel down both walls in a slow wave while he receives them with the same easy grin turned formal, and his glance finds the princess mid-ceremony and warms; the incense smoke leans and rights itself along the pillars, silks whispering as the wave of bows completes, and the camera drifts down the hall's center between the bowing rows

beats.visual: close at the foot of the phoenix throne: the gold crown of Baekje is lowered onto the boy's bowed head by an elder official's careful hands — the same sun-browned face beneath it, the topknot cord traded for a king's coil, the clever eyes lowered in the one solemn moment of his laughing life; incense climbs, the assembled hall holds its breath along the walls, and on the crown's front a small gold flower ornament catches the lamplight the way a pin at a collar once did; the yam-digger's hands rest open on his knees, and the crown settles
beats.motion: the crown lowers in the elder's careful hands through the incense light and settles onto the bowed head, the small gold flower on its front catching one steady gleam as it comes to rest; the hall's held breath releases in a long rustle of silk down both walls, his open hands closing slowly on his knees, and the camera holds the crowned bow in the drifting smoke

beats.visual: the old reedy pond at golden evening, empty of every person: the dug terraces have grown over green, across the still water white lotus flowers stand open in the last light — dozens of cups of pale light on the dark mirror; dragonflies stitch the warm air, reeds lean together at the banks, the eastern hills hold the last sun on their shoulders, and the quiet water keeps its gold and its story folded under the lotus leaves
beats.motion: only evening moves: the lotus cups swaying by a petal's width on the dark mirror, a dragonfly touching the water once so rings widen out through the reflected gold light, the reeds leaning together in the warm air; the hills darken by one shade, and the camera pulls back slowly and low across the blooming water
